help.precedence.title: # Operator precedence
help.precedence.status: The order below applies to mathematical expressions. Use parentheses to group a calculation explicitly.
help.precedence.conversionRule: `::` and `to` support the same conversions but apply to different parts of an expression. `::` binds before multiplication and addition. `to` applies after the arithmetic expression to its left.
help.precedence.continuedArithmetic: To continue arithmetic after `to`, use parentheses: `(2 to hex) + 3 = 5`. The intermediate representation does not change the number. `2 to hex + 3` asks for parentheses; `2::hex+3` is valid and produces `5`.
help.precedence.chainsRule: Consecutive conversions run from left to right, including mixed operators: `255 to hex::bin = 0b11111111`; `1 km to m::cm = 100 000 cm`. Each target names a conversion destination. The next conversion uses the preceding value, not the target name. The last target sets the final representation or unit. Rounded intermediate display text is never reused for calculation.
help.precedence.tableIntro: Higher rows bind first. Operators within an expression use this order unless parentheses explicitly change the grouping.
help.precedence.table.primary: | 1 | Parentheses, function calls, `√`, date/time literals, values with units (including compound durations) |
help.precedence.existingAssociativity: Already agreed: powers associate left to right, so `2^3^2 = (2^3)^2 = 64`. Power precedes unary minus: `-2^2 = -4`. Multiplication, implicit multiplication and division have equal priority and run left to right: `6/2(1+2) = 9`.
help.precedence.newOrderingExamples: Power and unary signs bind before `::`: `2^3::bin = 0b1000` and `-10::hex = -0xA`.
help.precedence.spacingRule: The operator determines precedence, regardless of spaces around it. `2+3::hex` and `2 + 3 :: hex` both produce `5`; `2+3 to hex` produces `0x5`. Spaces can still separate tokens or group decimal digits; they cannot be removed arbitrarily from every expression.
help.precedence.definitionRule: `=` defines a name; it is not an equality comparison. Evaluate its right-hand expression using the operator order. Use `==` for equality checks.
help.precedence.unitPowersRule: A final 2 or 3 on a complete known length-unit symbol automatically displays as a superscript: cm2 becomes cm², мм3 becomes мм³, ft2 becomes ft² and metre2 becomes metre². The same rule applies to explicit length aliases and to the Latin baseline plus one active locale. m2/m3 and м2/м3 always mean square/cubic metres, never minutes. Do not format a prefix of a longer name: m20 and m2rate remain unchanged; continuing the word removes the superscript formatting. Backspace immediately after m² deletes only the exponent, leaving m. Undo restores the preceding user input without an extra step for automatic formatting. Pasted formula text receives the same formatting as typed text: 2cm2 + 3cm2 displays as 2cm² + 3cm². One undo restores the state before the entire paste. Copying selected formula text puts the visible text on the clipboard, including actual ²/³ characters. Quick numeric result copy omits the unit and its superscript: 4m² copies 4. Displayed numeric rounding is preserved and the working value is unchanged. The caret ^ raises the entire quantity to a power: 2m2 denotes two square metres; 2m^2 leaves the supported answer 4m², discarding the squared-minutes interpretation. Unit support is checked after final cancellation. Shorthand autoformatting is not extended to time, mass or other dimensions.
help.precedence.comparisonChains: A chain such as `1 < x < 10` compares neighboring values and requires every comparison to hold. It means `1 < x and x < 10`. Stop at the first false comparison; do not compare a Boolean intermediate result with the next number.
help.precedence.lazyUnitsRule: Lowercase m can mean a metre or a minute; the active Russian spelling м follows the same rule. Lazy resolution uses the whole formula, including outer parentheses. If multiple interpretations remain valid, show all distinct visible answers: 10m / 2s gives 5m/s or the unitless 300. Identical-looking answers appear once: 2m * 2 displays one 4m. Answers have no interpretation captions and remain in one row with horizontal scrolling when needed. Grouping the display does not discard original meanings or exact values. Explicit metre and min select a unit directly; the Russian equivalents are метр and мин. For m and its local alias, metre interpretations precede minute interpretations.
help.precedence.durationNotation: Short duration symbols are w, d, h, m, s and ms. Russian symbols are н, д, ч, м, с and мс. Days remain 24 hours and weeks remain seven days. Adjacent duration components add, with or without spaces: 1h30m and 1h 30m both equal 90 minutes. Components may appear in any order and repeat: 30m1h equals 90 minutes; 1h30m15m equals 105 minutes. Use an explicit * to multiply adjacent duration quantities. With only ambiguous m symbols, retain both valid readings: 1m30m and 1m 30m give 31 minutes as a duration sum and 30 square metres as a length product. This does not introduce addition of adjacent lengths. A compound duration is one value for surrounding operators: 1h30m * 2 equals 180 minutes, and -1h30m equals minus 90 minutes. An incomplete final component such as 1h30 keeps the result blank until its unit is entered. An explicit operator is required before a following quantity of a clearly different dimension: 1h30m2km reports a missing operator; write 1h30m / 2km to calculate pace. This boundary does not remove the two accepted readings of 1m30m or other accepted forms of implicit multiplication.
result.alternatives.label: Possible results
help.precedence.simpleCompoundUnits: Supported compound units are speed (length/time, for example km/h), pace (time/length, min/km) and information-transfer rate (information/time, MB/s). Area and volume remain supported. Check support after final cancellation: (2s * 3s) / 1s = 6s is valid. Final units such as kg*m, s² and m/s² are excluded. Discard interpretations with unsupported final units and show the remaining valid answers; show the short unsupported-unit diagnostic only if no valid supported answer remains. Policies for other errors are still being specified. Temperature retains its separate conversion-only rule.
help.precedence.minRule: The min function takes at least two arguments separated by semicolons. One complete expression in the following parentheses denotes minutes multiplied by that expression: 2min(2+4) equals 12 minutes. With no coefficient, one minute is implied: min(2+4) = 1min(2+4), or 6 minutes. Two or more arguments denote the function: 2 min(2;4) = 2 * min(2;4) = 4, without a unit. Spaces before min do not change the meaning. Count arguments at the current parentheses level: 2min(max(2;4)) has one outer argument and equals 8 minutes. While 2min(2; is incomplete, the result stays blank. Closing it as 2min(2;) produces a missing-argument error, without reinterpreting the list as minutes. The max function also requires at least two arguments. Other malformed argument lists are still being specified.
completion.function.min.description: Smallest of two or more values.
completion.function.max.description: Largest of two or more values.
help.copy.quickRule: In the quick-mode formula editor with no text selected, press {shortcut} to copy the only displayed current result. Numeric results copy the displayed number without its unit: 4m copies 4. Rounding, all shown digits, grouping and numeral-system prefixes are preserved. With text selected, the shortcut copies that selection, including its unit text. Click a result to copy it. When several results are displayed, the editor has focus and no text is selected, the shortcut leaves the clipboard unchanged and prompts you to choose a result. The calculator stays open, your formula and cursor are preserved, and focus returns to input after a click. Quick copy does not add a history entry. Percentage results copy as decimal fractions: 30% copies 0.3 or 0,3 according to your number-format locale. Calendar answers copy their complete shown date, time, day carry and any shown offset. A calendar period with a nonzero month component is also copied in full, including its units; an ordinary fixed duration still copies only its numeric coefficient. An answer shown as ≈ 0 is ready to copy and copies 0; any unit or percent sign stays only in its display. Its working value remains nonzero.
help.confirm.quickRule: With one ready displayed result in quick mode, press {shortcut} to record the calculation in history and copy the result. After both succeed, a new empty input starts in the same place, expanded history collapses and the calculator stays open. Arrow Up opens history again with the newest calculation nearest to the input. If saving history or copying fails, the formula and result remain and a brief error appears; the input is not cleared, history does not collapse and the window stays open. Numeric results are copied without units, using the displayed number. Ordinary quick copy keeps your current input and does not add history. Percentage results copy as decimal fractions: 30% copies 0.3 or 0,3 according to your number-format locale.
history.save.error: Could not save the calculation to history. Try again.
help.confirm.hideRule: With one ready displayed result in quick mode, press {shortcut} to record the calculation in history, copy the result and hide the calculator after both succeed. The next invocation starts with empty input. If saving history or copying fails, the formula and result remain, a brief error appears and the window stays open.
help.confirm.retryRule: If confirmation fails, retry without changing the formula, result or chosen answer to finish the same calculation. An entry already saved to history will not be added again. After saving and copying succeed, the command used for the retry determines whether the calculator stays open with empty input or hides until the next invocation. If you choose a different answer after a failed confirmation and confirm it, that is a new confirmation. Any entry already saved with the previous choice remains unchanged. The pending quick calculation keeps the same clock snapshot. Escape cancels the wait, keeps the window open and refreshes the calculation; editing also cancels. Saved history remains. Hiding and reopening preserves the wait within the session. Ordinary copy failures and sheet copying do not freeze the calculation.
help.confirm.multipleRule: When quick mode shows several results, press {confirmShortcut} or {hideShortcut} to focus the result row. The first answer is highlighted, but nothing is copied or saved yet. Use Left Arrow and Right Arrow to choose; the row scrolls when needed and stops at either end without wrapping. Up Arrow and Down Arrow leave result selection and immediately navigate history as usual, without copying or confirming. Press {confirmShortcut} again to record the calculation and copy the chosen answer, then start empty input with history collapsed. Press {hideShortcut} instead to confirm and hide the calculator. Escape returns the cursor to its previous position in the formula without changes. Clicking an answer still only copies it and returns focus to input. Typing, pasting, Backspace or Delete returns you to the formula at the previous cursor or text selection and performs the usual edit. This ends result selection and recalculates without copying or recording; Backspace and Delete edit formula text, not history.
help.history.recordRule: History keeps the formula, all its results and the answer chosen when you confirmed the calculation. Copying one answer does not remove the others. Saved results do not change when you edit a constant or function. When you bring a formula back into input, it is calculated again using the current definitions; the original history entry stays unchanged. Bringing a formula back into input does not itself add a new history entry. Each new successful confirmation adds a separate history entry, even for an identical calculation. Retrying an unfinished confirmation after an error does not duplicate its saved entry. If a saved definition was renamed, recalling its formula uses the current name of that same definition; the original history text and answers remain unchanged. After a definition is deleted, recalculation may require restoring it or correcting the formula.
help.history.displayRule: Each history row shows the formula and all its saved results. With several results, the answer chosen at confirmation is bold. Long rows scroll horizontally. Moving through history does not change the saved choice.
history.clear.description: This will clear your calculation history. Your constants, functions, sheets and templates will be kept. You can undo the clearing until you fully quit the application.
help.history.searchRule: In quick mode, press {shortcut} to search history by formula or saved result. Type any part of a formula or saved displayed result; matching ignores letter case. Matches update as you type and keep the normal history order. An empty query shows all history. Up Arrow and Down Arrow choose a record while preserving your formula. Enter closes search and brings the chosen formula into input for recalculation without confirming or copying it. Escape closes search and restores your previous formula and cursor. With no matches, Enter recalls nothing. The formula input stays in place, and searching does not recalculate saved results.
help.history.manageRule: Deleting one history entry requires no confirmation. Clearing the entire history requires confirmation. Undo restores deletions in reverse order; clearing the entire history counts as one operation. You can undo until you fully quit the application. Hiding and reopening the window keeps Undo available. Restoring removed entries keeps calculations added later. These actions preserve your constants, functions, sheets and templates. History Undo is separate from undoing formula text edits.
help.history.retentionRule: Your history is kept between application launches until you delete it. Old entries are not removed automatically because of their age or the number of saved calculations. Undo for deletions and clearing is available only until you fully quit the application.
help.history.searchNotationRule: History search treats 1,5 and 1.5, and 1000 and 1 000, as equivalent number spellings. It also matches unit spellings such as m2 and m², or cm3 and cm³, in either direction. Caret powers such as 2m^2 remain distinct from unit shorthand such as 2m2. Search can match any saved displayed answer as well as the formula.
help.history.menuRule: In quick mode, right-click a history entry or press {shortcut} to open the history menu. Use formula and Delete entry apply to a chosen record. Undo restores the last deletion or clearing operation. Clear history asks for confirmation. The shortcut also works when history is collapsed or empty; record actions require a selected entry. Opening the menu leaves your formula unchanged. Escape closes it and restores the previous focus.
help.copy.focusedResultRule: While the current result row has focus, press {shortcut} to copy the highlighted answer. Numbers copy without units, using the displayed formatting. Focus and selection stay on that answer; your formula, cursor and window are preserved, and no history entry is added. You can then press Enter to confirm or Escape to return to the formula. A text selection left in the editor does not change which answer is copied. Percentage results copy as decimal fractions: 30% copies 0.3 or 0,3 according to your number-format locale. Calendar answers copy their complete shown date, time, day carry and any shown offset. A calendar period with a nonzero month component is also copied in full, including its units; an ordinary fixed duration still copies only its numeric coefficient. An answer shown as ≈ 0 is ready to copy and copies 0; any unit or percent sign stays only in its display. Its working value remains nonzero.
help.history.copyRule: Click an answer in history to copy its saved displayed value. Numbers copy without units, retaining displayed formatting; logical answers copy their displayed text. Your current formula and cursor are preserved, focus returns to input and the calculator stays open. This does not recalculate, confirm, add a history entry or change the answer chosen at confirmation. If a saved calculation shows price * 2 = 200, clicking its answer copies 200 even if the current price would give 300. Use formula brings the expression into input for a new calculation. Percentage results copy as decimal fractions: 30% copies 0.3 or 0,3 according to your number-format locale. Calendar answers copy their complete shown date, time, day carry and any shown offset. A calendar period with a nonzero month component is also copied in full, including its units; an ordinary fixed duration still copies only its numeric coefficient. An answer shown as ≈ 0 is ready to copy and copies 0; any unit or percent sign stays only in its display. Its working value remains nonzero.
help.history.navigationRule: In quick mode, Up Arrow opens history and immediately brings the preceding calculation into input. Press Up again to recall older entries while the list moves downward through the fixed input. Down Arrow moves back through the entries until it restores the text you had before browsing, even if that text was not empty. Recalled formulas are calculated again using the current definitions; saved history entries stay unchanged. Returning to your original input restores its cursor and collapses history. Up stops at the oldest entry, and further Down at your original input does not clear it.
help.input.undoRule: Each formula recalled from history and each Down Arrow return to your original input is one text-undo step. Press {shortcut} to restore the previous text and cursor; the formula is recalculated with the current definitions. This also applies when you use a search result or Use formula. A new empty input after successful confirmation starts a separate undo chain. Undo does not remove saved calculations or undo a clipboard copy. Hiding the window keeps text undo available; fully quitting ends that chain. Copying a sheet result does not start a new text-undo chain.
help.quick.restoreRule: After you fully quit and reopen the application, quick mode restores your last input and cursor, with history collapsed and focus in the input. The formula is calculated again using the current definitions. If your last input was empty, it stays empty. Text undo from the previous application session is not restored. Simply hiding and reopening the window keeps the current text-undo chain.
help.results.orderRule: Possible answers follow a fixed interpretation order. For m, metre comes before minute; ambiguous occurrences are considered from left to right. Thus 10m / 2s shows 5m/s before 300. Removing invalid alternatives keeps the remaining order; identical displayed answers share the position of their first alternative. Changing numbers or the interface language does not sort answers into a different order.
help.history.extendedShortcutRule: In expanded mode, press {shortcut} with either modifier key to open history while keeping your sheet unchanged. Up Arrow and Down Arrow choose a record; Left Arrow and Right Arrow choose its saved answer. Start at the latest record and its answer chosen at confirmation; when you change records, select that record’s confirmation choice. Navigation stops at the ends and scrolls the selected item into view. Press {copyShortcut} to copy the saved answer without recalculation and keep focus in history. Enter closes history and inserts the formula at your previous cursor, replacing selected text, as one ordinary edit. The sheet recalculates without confirming or adding history. Escape or {shortcut} again closes history without insertion and restores the previous cursor. Empty history provides nothing to select or insert. Ordinary arrows retain text-editor behavior while editing. References to renamed saved definitions use their current names in the inserted formula; the history record stays unchanged. Percentage results copy as decimal fractions: 30% copies 0.3 or 0,3 according to your number-format locale.
help.sheet.dependenciesRule: In a calculation sheet, define each local variable once. Expressions may reference definitions farther down the sheet: total = price * quantity can precede price = 100 and quantity = 3 and still gives 300. Editing a definition recalculates its dependent expressions. Defining the same local name again is an error. Circular dependencies block the expressions in the cycle and those that depend on them; independent expressions still calculate. Multiline user-function bodies keep their sequential execution rules.
sheet.duplicateVariable: Variable {name} is defined more than once in this sheet.
sheet.dependencyError: A required value could not be calculated.
help.sheet.resultsRule: Each completed expression or assignment in a calculation sheet shows its own result. For example, price = 100 shows 100 and price * 3 shows 300. Blank lines and comments have no result. If an expression has several valid answers, show them all using the existing grouping, ordering and horizontal-scrolling rules.
help.sheet.scopeRule: Local variables belong to their calculation sheet. They do not become saved definitions in quick mode or other sheets. A local variable takes precedence over a saved constant with the same name inside that sheet without changing the saved constant. If the global price is 50 and a sheet defines price = 100, that sheet uses 100 while quick mode still uses 50. Built-in names remain protected. A sheet-local name cannot match a saved function name. Saved functions do not implicitly use the calling sheet’s local variables.
help.sheet.autosaveRule: You can keep several named calculation sheets. Their text is saved automatically on this computer, including unfinished or erroneous expressions. Autosaving does not add calculation-history entries. Reopening a sheet restores its text and calculates it again using the current saved constants and functions. Saving a template and saving a global constant or function remain separate actions.
help.sheet.copyRule: In the sheet editor, Enter inserts a new line. With text selected, {copyShortcut} copies the selection. Without a selection, it copies the only ready displayed answer of the expression containing the cursor. If that expression has several answers, the clipboard stays unchanged and you are prompted to choose a result. Click an answer to copy it. Press {resultShortcut} to copy the current expression’s single answer or focus its result row to choose with Left and Right. In that row, Enter or {resultShortcut} copies the chosen answer and returns to the previous editor cursor; {copyShortcut} copies it while keeping row focus. Escape returns without copying. Typing, paste, Backspace or Delete resumes normal editing at the previous cursor or selection. Numeric answers copy the displayed number without units, preserving shown rounding, digits, sign, grouping and base prefix and case. Logical answers copy their visible localized text. Missing, invalid or stale answers cannot be copied. The sheet stays open and is not cleared. Copying, recalculation and autosave do not add history entries or reset text undo. Percentage results copy as decimal fractions: 30% copies 0.3 or 0,3 according to your number-format locale. Calendar answers copy their complete shown date, time, day carry and any shown offset. A calendar period with a nonzero month component is also copied in full, including its units; an ordinary fixed duration still copies only its numeric coefficient. An answer shown as ≈ 0 is ready to copy and copies 0; any unit or percent sign stays only in its display. Its working value remains nonzero.
help.sheet.errorRule: An expression with an error or incomplete input has no ready result. Expressions depending on it also have no ready answer; independent expressions continue calculating. For a = 1 / 0, b = a + 1 and c = 2 + 2, a has an error, b cannot obtain its dependency and c is 4. An unknown-name message identifies the name. Previous values are never presented as current results. The sheet still saves your text. Unused branches of if, and and or are not evaluated.
help.definitions.functionScopeRule: A saved function uses its parameters, its own local intermediate names and saved global definitions. It does not implicitly use the calling sheet’s local variables. With global price = 50 and cost(x) = x * price, a sheet-local price = 100 does not change cost(2): the answer is 100. To use a sheet value inside a function, pass it as an argument. Arguments are calculated in the caller’s context before they bind to parameters. Multiline function bodies run in order.
help.definitions.constantRule: A saved constant retains its definition formula and its dependencies on other saved constants. With rate = 20% and factor = 1 + rate, explicitly saving rate as 10% changes factor to 1.1. Editing a draft does not change the saved definition before you save it. Cyclic definitions are not allowed.
help.definitions.saveRule: Edit a saved definition as a draft, then choose Save to apply it. A valid saved change updates future calculations and recalculates current quick input and open dependent sheets. Invalid syntax, unknown references, recursion or cyclic dependencies keep the previous working version; your edits remain available to correct. A valid function may still fail for particular arguments: f(x) = 1 / x fails at zero. The description from the header’s first # comment is saved with the definition. Existing history answers do not recalculate.
help.definitions.namesRule: Each global name identifies one saved constant or function. Functions cannot share a name by accepting different numbers of arguments. Creating a definition does not overwrite an existing one; open it explicitly to edit. A sheet-local variable may shadow a saved constant, but it cannot use a saved function’s name. Built-in names remain protected.
help.definitions.renameRule: Renaming a saved definition updates references to it in other saved definitions, sheets and templates. Unrelated local names and comments are unchanged. History keeps its original formula and answers; recalling the formula for a new calculation uses the definition’s current name. Renaming price to cost leaves price * 2 in history but recalls cost * 2. Reusing the old name for another definition does not redirect those references. Name conflicts are checked before the rename; a rename cannot be partially applied.
help.definitions.deleteRule: A definition cannot be deleted while other saved definitions, sheets or templates use it; the calculator shows where it is used. History alone does not prevent deletion and retains its saved answers. Recalculating an old formula may require restoring the definition or correcting the formula. An unused definition is deleted without an extra confirmation dialog and can be restored with the definition library’s Undo until you fully quit. Hiding the window keeps Undo available. If a new definition now uses the same name, restoration reports the conflict and does not overwrite the new data.
definitions.inUse: {name} is used by other definitions, sheets or templates.
definitions.nameConflict: The name {name} is already used by a saved definition.
definitions.invalid: The definition has errors. Your edits are kept; the working version is unchanged.
definitions.restoreConflict: Cannot restore {name}: a new definition uses that name.
sheet.functionNameConflict: {name} is a saved function name and cannot be a sheet variable.
help.library.rule: Press {shortcut} inside the calculator to find sheets, templates and saved definitions in one library, grouped by type. Search by name; definitions can also be found by their descriptions from # comments. Enter opens a sheet, starts a template or opens a definition for editing. Creation and management actions are available here too.
help.templates.rule: Save a copy of a sheet as a template and choose its local parameter variables and default values. Starting the template with parameter values creates an independent named sheet with autosave. Editing that sheet does not change the template. Updating the template is explicit and does not rewrite sheets already created from it. References to saved global constants and functions remain live.
help.documents.manageRule: Create, rename, duplicate or delete sheets and templates from their management actions. Closing a sheet keeps it saved; a duplicate has its own text. Deleting one document does not require an extra confirmation dialog and can be undone until you fully quit. Hiding the window keeps document deletion Undo available. Other documents, history and definitions are preserved, and restoration does not overwrite newer data. This Undo is separate from text editing and history deletion Undo.
help.data.exportRule: A full export puts sheets, templates, saved definitions and shared settings such as theme, language and copy behavior into one portable file. History is not included and stays on this device. The global invocation shortcut, autostart and window placement also stay device-local. The file preserves calculation references, unit meanings and your own text for transfer between Windows and macOS. No account or cloud synchronization is required.
help.data.selectedExportRule: Export selected sheets, templates or definitions together with the saved constants and functions they need, including further dependencies. Unrelated history and other data are not included. Incomplete sheet text can still be transferred; missing definitions are not invented.
help.data.importRule: Preview additions and conflicts before importing. Importing the same unchanged object again does not duplicate it. A differing version that conflicts with an existing object is added as a separately named copy by default, with its internal references adjusted together. Existing objects are not overwritten. The file’s structure, version and reference integrity are checked before applying the import as one change. A damaged or unsupported file leaves your data unchanged. An incomplete sheet formula alone does not make the file damaged. Shared settings change only if you select Apply settings in the preview; the option starts unchecked.
help.data.backupRule: The calculator keeps full local snapshots of data and settings, including history, when data change at most once a day, and also before import or restore. It retains the latest ten copies. If current data can be read, restoring a chosen backup explicitly returns that saved state after a preview and a successful backup of your current state. Damaged-data recovery first preserves the original files separately. Ordinary startup does not bring back deleted history. The ten-backup limit does not limit your main calculation history.
library.title: Library
templates.parameters.title: Parameters
data.export.description: Export sheets, templates, definitions and shared settings. History stays on this device.
help.templates.parametersRule: Before creating a sheet from a template, fill in the compact parameter fields, already populated with defaults. Use the normal expression language, including numbers, units and saved constants or functions: 100000, 2 * 50000 or rate. Creating the sheet stores your entered expressions in its corresponding local definitions. An incomplete or invalid parameter is marked and prevents finishing the launch. Cancel creates no sheet and leaves the template unchanged. The new sheet keeps its usual live calculation and global dependencies.
help.data.importSettingsRule: Import adds calculations and definitions while keeping your current settings by default. Select Apply settings in the preview to see and apply changes to shared preferences such as theme, language and copy behavior. The option starts unchecked. Device-specific invocation, autostart and window placement are not in the transfer file.
help.data.restoreRule: A local backup contains the full saved data and settings, including history. When current data can be read, restoring it returns the chosen state: the preview shows additions, changes and current items that will disappear. Before applying it, the calculator must successfully back up your current state. If that backup cannot be saved, restoration does not start. This explicit restore can bring back the history in the chosen snapshot; ordinary startup does not. Portable export still excludes history, and import keeps its separate conflict-copy rules.
help.data.saveFailureRule: If a sheet cannot be saved, its text remains available in the current session with a Not saved status and a retry action. An incomplete or erroneous formula is not itself a save failure. Hiding the window keeps your text available. Fully quitting with these unsaved edits offers saving the text separately or explicitly exiting without saving. After an application crash, recover the last successfully saved state; edits that never reached storage cannot be promised. If saving a global definition fails, its previous published version remains and the draft stays available to correct.
help.documents.restoreRule: Undoing a sheet or template deletion restores its text and references without reverting the global library. If a required definition has since been deleted, the document shows the missing dependency. Restore that definition with its own Undo when available, or correct the formula. An unrelated new definition with the same name is not substituted automatically. Deleted documents kept only for Undo do not count as active uses that block definition deletion.
data.restore.backupError: Could not back up the current state. Restore has not started.
data.unsaved.exitDescription: Save your text to a separate file, or exit without saving these changes.
expression.missingDefinition: The referenced definition {name} is no longer available.
help.finance.ratesRule: The convenient monthly forms use an annual nominal rate and a number of months: 12% annually means 1% for each calculation month. The general forms take a rate per period and a number of periods. Enter rates as ordinary expressions such as 12% or 0.12; the number 12 is not automatically interpreted as 12%. A zero rate is valid. An effective annual rate is not silently treated as a nominal rate, and financial months do not introduce calendar arithmetic.
help.finance.loanRule: A loan is fully repaid through equal periodic payments at a constant rate. Payments are at the end of each period by default; the beginning can be specified explicitly. Enter the loan amount as a positive amount; the returned payment is a positive amount too. Separate calculations provide the payment, total repayments and overpayment, which is total repayments minus the loan principal. At a zero rate, the payment is the loan amount divided by the number of payments. Fees and contract-specific rules are not added automatically.
help.finance.savingsRule: Calculate savings from an initial amount, a constant rate and an equal contribution each period. The contribution is optional and defaults to zero; the initial amount may also be zero. Contributions occur at the end of the period by default, with the beginning available explicitly. Separate calculations return the accumulated amount and interest earned: the total minus the initial amount and all your contributions. At a zero rate, the total is simply the initial amount plus all contributions.
help.finance.roiRule: Provide the total invested, including costs, and the total returned, including returned capital and additional receipts. Profit is returned money minus invested money. ROI is profit divided by investment, shown as a percentage for the whole period. Investing 100000 and receiving 130000 gives a profit of 30000 and ROI of 30%. Losses and negative ROI are valid, with no automatic annualization. ROI is undefined at zero investment; profit can still be calculated separately. Costs already included in investment are not subtracted again. Copying a percentage result uses its decimal fraction: 30% copies 0.3 or 0,3.
help.finance.paybackRule: Use the initial investment and a constant net cash inflow per period. Net cash flow is cash received minus cash paid. One calculation estimates a fractional payback time for cash arriving evenly within each period; another returns the number of complete periods when the entire payment arrives only at period end. An investment of 100000 with 30000 per period gives 10/3 periods or 4 complete periods, respectively. A positive investment with zero or negative net inflow does not pay back and has no ready numeric answer. With zero investment, either calculation returns zero periods.
help.finance.precisionRule: Financial calculations use the same 30 significant digits and normal result display as other calculations. Each accrual or payment is not secretly rounded to cents. Use round(...; 2) explicitly when you want to round the final expression to two decimal places. Total repayments and earned interest are calculated from working values, not rounded text on screen. This does not create a contract-specific payment schedule with rounding at every step. Computed fractional results use 30 significant digits with exact ties rounded away from zero; subsequent operations use that working value.
help.finance.conditionsRule: Monetary inputs are amounts in one currency. Exchange rates, taxes, fees and rules of a particular bank are not inserted automatically. Include the expenses and conditions you need through explicit expressions, your own functions or a calculation sheet.
completion.finance.loanOverpayment.descr: Total repayments minus the loan principal.
completion.finance.savingsInterest.descr: Accumulated amount minus your initial sum and contributions.
completion.finance.profit.description: Total returned minus total invested, including costs.
completion.finance.roi.description: Profit as a percentage of investment for the whole period.
completion.finance.paybackEstimate.descr: Fractional payback estimate for an even net cash inflow.
completion.finance.paybackWholePeriods.d: Complete periods until period-end cash receipts cover investment.
finance.roi.zeroInvestment: ROI is undefined when investment is zero.
help.copy.percentRule: A percentage result copies as a decimal fraction without the percent sign. For example, 30% copies 0.3 with a decimal point or 0,3 with a decimal comma. This applies to result shortcuts, clicks, confirmation and saved history answers. Selected formula text, including 30%, is copied literally. Copying does not change the working percentage value. For a rounded percentage, divide the displayed coefficient by 100 without adding hidden digits or rounding again: 33.3333333333% copies 0.333333333333. Moving the decimal point can produce more fractional places in the clipboard than the screen shows.
help.finance.argumentsRule: Loan functions take (amount; annual_rate; months; timing?), and savings functions take (initial_amount; annual_rate; months; contribution?; timing?). The _period forms take a rate per period and a period count in the same positions. Contribution defaults to 0 and timing to end; start means the beginning of the period. Pass 0 explicitly before timing if there is no contribution. profit and roi take (invested; returned); both payback functions take (invested; net_cash_flow). The ? marks optional arguments in help only. Calls use positional arguments separated by semicolons.
help.finance.boundsRule: Loan amounts and whole period counts must be positive. Savings amounts and whole period counts may be zero but cannot be negative. Fractional counts are rejected, not rounded. A rate per period must be greater than -100%; monthly forms check the annual nominal rate after dividing it by 12. Monetary inputs are dimensionless amounts in one currency. Profit allows nonnegative investment and return; ROI requires positive investment. Payback allows zero investment and then returns zero periods.
help.finance.rateConversionRule: effective(annual_rate; compounds_per_year) converts an annual nominal rate to an effective annual rate. nominal(annual_rate; compounds_per_year) converts back. The compounding count is required and must be a positive integer. Both results are percentages. For example, effective(12%; 12) is approximately 12.6825%. The nominal rate per compounding period and the effective annual rate must each be greater than -100% for their respective conversion. These functions do not change the rate convention of a monthly calculation.
help.percent.displayRule: A percentage value is displayed with %: entering 10% shows 10%, and ROI of 30% shows 30%. Its numerical meaning is still the decimal fraction, and 200 + 10% is still 220. Entering the ordinary fraction 0.1 does not automatically make it a percentage. Percentage results copy as decimal fractions. Multiplication and division with numbers or percentages produce an ordinary number: 200 * 10% = 10% * 200 = 20 and 10% * 2 = 0.2. Therefore 200 + 10% * 2 gives 200.2; write 200 + (10 * 2)% to get 240. Sums and differences of rates retain their percent sign. A percentage on the left of an ordinary number uses its fraction: 10% + 200 = 200.1 and 10% - 200 = -199.9. A percentage on the right still gives the relative change: 200 + 10% = 220.
help.values.timingRule: You can store a payment or contribution timing value in a constant or variable and pass it through your functions. For example, timing = start can supply the last argument of savings. start and end are distinct symbolic values, not numbers 0 and 1. Compare them with == or !=; ordering and arithmetic are not supported. On its own, a timing result displays and copies its localized symbol.
help.values.booleanRule: Use true and false as logical values. Comparisons also produce logical values, displayed and copied as Yes or No. if, and, or and not require logical conditions; 0 and 1 are not automatically treated as false and true. Arithmetic such as true + 2 is an error.
help.evaluation.alternativesRule: If one interpretation of an ambiguous formula fails numerically while another succeeds, show the valid answers. For example, a division-by-zero or invalid-function-argument interpretation does not hide a valid result from another interpretation. If no valid answer remains, show a brief error. Incomplete input remains incomplete, and an unselected conditional branch is not evaluated.
help.evaluation.bindingRule: Repeated uses of one named value keep the same interpretation within a calculation. If a = 1m, then a / a is 1 whether a means a metre or a minute; it does not mix the two meanings. Passing that value as a function argument preserves the connection. Separate unit occurrences written directly in a formula remain independent. A later independent calculation can resolve the stored formula using its new context.
help.evaluation.validationRule: Syntax and name references are checked throughout the expression, but only the selected conditional branch is evaluated numerically. if(2 > 1; 4; 1/0) returns 4. if(2 > 1; 4; unknown_name) reports the unknown name even though that branch would not be selected. Incomplete input has no ready result.
help.calendar.dateInputRule: Enter dates as YYYY-MM-DD in any interface language; Russian also accepts DD.MM.YYYY. Use two digits for month and day and four for year. A complete date is recognized before subtraction: 2026-10-09 is a date, while 2026 - 10 - 09 is subtraction. A nonexistent date is an error; an incomplete date has no ready result. Other regional formats are not guessed. Supported years are 0001–9999; values outside this range are errors.
help.calendar.timeInputRule: Enter time in 24-hour form: 14:30, 14:30:25 or 14:30:25.123. Seconds are optional, and a fractional second may have one to three digits after a point or comma. Join a date and time with a space or T: 2026-10-09 14:30 or 2026-10-09T14:30. Use 00:00 for the start of a day; 24:00 and AM/PM are not accepted.
help.calendar.dynamicRule: today, yesterday and tomorrow return dates; now returns the current date and time. Enter these names without parentheses and use them in formulas, sheets, constants or your functions. The Latin names always work; the active interface language also supplies its localized names. These built-in names cannot be redefined.
help.calendar.refreshRule: Each calculation uses one clock snapshot. Visible formulas depending on the current date refresh when the date changes; those depending on current time refresh every second. Opening the calculator again, waking the computer, or changing system time or zone refreshes affected active calculations. A saved formula using today stays dynamic. Historical answers remain saved values. Copy and confirmation use the ready answer already shown, without an extra hidden recalculation. After a partially failed quick confirmation, the shown snapshot waits for retry. Escape keeps the window open and resumes a fresh calculation; editing also cancels the wait. Hiding and reopening preserves the pending snapshot until a full restart.
help.calendar.arithmeticRule: Add or subtract durations from dates and date-times, and compare or subtract calendar values. 2026-10-09 + 4w3d gives 2026-11-09. Adding whole days to a date keeps a date; a fractional day starts from 00:00 and produces a date-time. A difference between dates is a number of days. Times without dates use the same reference day: 01:00 - 23:00 is -22h. A time crossing midnight retains its day carry: 23:30 + 2h gives 01:30 (+1d).
help.calendar.monthsRule: Calendar months and years are separate from fixed-duration units. If the target month lacks the original day, use its last day: 31 January 2026 plus one month is 28 February 2026, and 29 February 2024 plus one year is 28 February 2025. Explicit additions run in order: adding one month twice from 31 January gives 28 March, while adding two months at once gives 31 March. A month cannot become a fixed number of days without a starting date. Write months as mon and years as y; Russian also accepts мес and год. For example, 2026-01-31 + 1mon + 1mon gives 2026-03-28, while 2026-01-31 + 2mon gives 2026-03-31.
help.calendar.offsetRule: UTC and fixed numeric offsets are supported for date-times. If no offset is supplied, use the current system offset shared by the calculation, not a historical or future offset chosen from the entered date. A date without time has no offset. Days are always 24 hours and weeks are seven days; seasonal clock changes are ignored. Append Z or ±HH:mm to a time, with or without a space. Convert with to UTC, ::UTC, or a target such as UTC+01:00. For example, 2026-10-09 14:30+03:00 to UTC gives 2026-10-09 11:30Z. Offset hours are 00–23 and minutes 00–59. Both signed zero offsets display Z. Explicit offsets stay visible; an implicit system offset is not added to the shown answer. The same notation works for a time without a date and keeps its day carry.
help.calendar.copyRule: Calendar answers display dates as YYYY-MM-DD in every language and times in 24-hour form, joining date and time with a space. Keep nonzero seconds and fractional parts; do not add unnecessary zeros. Copy the entire shown answer, including its date, time, day carry and any shown fixed offset. Do not turn it into a numeric timestamp. Selected formula text is copied literally; saved historical answers are not recalculated. Computed time is rounded only for display to the nearest millisecond, with exact ties toward the later time and a point before fractional seconds. A calendar period is copied with all its displayed components and units; fixed durations keep their ordinary numeric-only copy rule.
help.precedence.calendarLiteralsRule: A complete 2026-10-09 is one date value. Write 2026 - 10 - 09 to subtract numbers. Russian also accepts 09.10.2026 as a date. A nonexistent complete date is an error, and an incomplete date has no ready result. Time such as 14:30 and date-time such as 2026-10-09 14:30 are also whole values. These token rules do not change the priority of ::, to or arithmetic operators. An offset suffix belongs to the value: 2026-10-09 14:30+03:00. UTC+01:00 is one conversion target. A carried clock such as 01:30Z (+1d) is one value, not multiplication by parentheses. Adjacent calendar components such as 1mon1d also form one period; its months are applied once, then its fixed duration. Separate + operators still apply sequentially.
help.calendar.periodRule: Combine calendar and fixed units in one period: 1y2mon3d. Its years and months are combined and applied once, then its fixed duration. Repeating or reordering components inside the same period does not change it. 2026-01-30 + 1mon1d gives 2026-03-01. Store periods by name, add or subtract compatible components, and multiply or divide the whole period by a number. Fractional months may be intermediate values, but the total must be a whole number when applied to a date: 0.5y is 6mon; 0.5mon is not guessed to mean 15d.
help.calendar.periodOutputRule: A calendar period shows years, months and fixed-duration components in descending order, omitting zeros and grouping each complete twelve months into a year. Opposing parts keep explicit signs. Copy includes all shown components and units. If the total month component becomes zero, the result is an ordinary fixed duration. Converting a calendar period to a fixed number of days requires a starting date.
help.calendar.mixedValuesRule: Add a date and a clock time in either order to combine them: 2026-10-09 + 14:30 gives 2026-10-09 14:30. Keep any carried days and explicit clock offset; otherwise use the shared system offset. When subtracting or comparing a date and a date-time, the date means 00:00 at that system offset. A clock time alone needs a supplied date before comparison with a dated value.
help.calendar.carryRule: You can enter or paste a carried time such as 01:30 (+1d) again. The signed day count must be an integer; negative and multiple-day carries work too. Use d or the active local day symbol. If an offset is present, it comes before the carry: 01:30Z (+1d). Zero carry is hidden. The whole form is a time value, not implicit multiplication.
help.calendar.precisionRule: Calculated time keeps finer working fractions and rounds only its final display to the nearest millisecond. Exact ties choose the later time; carry propagates through midnight and the date. Thus 00:00 + 0.4ms + 0.4ms displays 00:00:00.001. A duration alone, 0.4ms + 0.4ms, still gives 0.8ms. Display and copy use a point and at most three fractional-second digits in every language. No 24:00 or date outside years 0001–9999 is displayed. This does not change the numeric round function.
calendar.fractionalMonths: A date needs a whole number of months.
help.numeric.workingPrecisionRule: Enter at most 30 significant digits. Computed fractional results are rounded to 30 significant digits, with exact ties away from zero; later operations use that working value. Decimal operations that fit the precision stay exact, such as 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3. The ten fractional places on screen do not round the working value. Integers outside the 30-decimal-digit magnitude limit are errors, not rounded values.
help.numeric.smallValueRule: If ten fractional places would turn a nonzero answer into zero, extend its ordinary decimal form to three significant digits, but no more than 30 fractional places. Do not add unnecessary zeros or switch to scientific notation. For example, 0.000000000012345 displays 0.0000000000123. If even this limit rounds it to zero, show ≈ 0. The working value remains nonzero, so later calculations can still use it. Fractional digits after the second remain dimmed. An answer shown as ≈ 0 is ready to copy and copies 0; any unit or percent sign stays only in its display. Its working value remains nonzero. This display rule applies only within the supported working-number range.
help.calendar.periodComparisonRule: Calendar periods are equal when their normalized month totals and fixed-duration parts are equal: 1y == 12mon is true, 1mon == 30d is false, and (1mon + 3d) == (1mon + 72h) is true. Order pure months or years by their month totals and fixed durations by their lengths. Ordering a mixed period, or a calendar period against a fixed duration, needs a starting date. Apply both to that date, then compare the results; do not assume a month is 30 days.
help.numeric.approximateZeroActionsRule: An approximately-zero answer is ready: clicking it or using the result-copy shortcut copies 0. Keep its normal suffix on screen, such as ≈ 0 m or ≈ 0%. Quick confirmation saves the real nonzero value and starts a new input after the usual successful save and copy; modified confirmation hides the window. Exact 0 and ≈ 0 remain different visible answers. Identical approximate answers group under the normal rules without losing their underlying values. Sheets keep their normal copy behavior; selected source text is literal.
help.numeric.typePreservingAbsRule: abs preserves the kind of value: abs(-1cm) gives a length equal to 1cm and abs(-50%) gives 50%. General numeric operations transform the reference number while retaining the type. The final display may automatically choose a suitable unit scale. Specific operations define their own result-type or dimensional rules.
help.numeric.referenceRoundingRule: round, floor and ceil operate on a value’s reference number and preserve its type and scale context. round(12.345%; 2) rounds 0.12345 to 0.12 and displays 12%. floor(1234mm) has a reference result of 1 metre and displays 1000mm, preserving the sole mm scale. To round the written rate coefficient instead, use round(12.345% * 100; 2)%, which gives 12.35%.
help.numeric.typedRootsRule: Powers and roots have specific type rules: a squared length is an area, and sqrt(4m²) gives a length of 2m. A standalone sqrt(4m) has no supported result unit. Percentage powers and roots produce ordinary numbers: (50%)^2 = 0.25 and sqrt(25%) = 0.5. The existing rules for simplifying intermediate units and validating final units still apply.
help.numeric.measuredCombinationsRule: Adding or subtracting a bare number and a measurement requires a unit for the number: 1cm + 2 is invalid. Percentages can scale a measurement: 100cm * 50% and 50% * 100cm give a length of 50cm; 100cm + 10% gives a length of 110cm. A percentage on the left does not become a measurement automatically: 10% + 100cm is invalid. Final display may select another scale for the same measured value.
help.numeric.functionTypeRules: min and max compare compatible reference values and return the selected value with its type; equal values select the first argument. For example, min(50%; 0.6) gives 50%. Logarithms and trigonometry accept ordinary numbers and percentage fractions, plus the already supported angles for trigonometry. Length, area, mass and duration are not accepted just because they have a reference number. ln(100%) = 0, while sin(1cm) is invalid. Results are ordinary numbers except the already defined angular inverse-trigonometric results.
help.units.automaticScaleRule: An explicit conversion target chooses the result unit. Otherwise, keep a single scale used in the expression. With several scales, choose the coefficient with the fewest fractional decimal places before screen rounding, ignoring trailing zeros; ties choose the larger unit. 1m + 100mm gives 1100mm; 1m + 1000mm gives 2m; 1km + 1mm gives 1 000 001mm. This also applies to functions, information, fixed durations and derived-unit numerators: floor(1234mm) gives 1000mm and 90s remains 90s. Names and functions carry scale context; min and max use the selected value. Full automatic scale ladders are used only without inherited scale context. Ordinary measurement copy uses the shown numeric coefficient without its unit.
expression.incompatibleValueTypes: These values cannot be used together in this operation.
help.precedence.unitTargetsRule: A conversion target is a unit or a supported ratio of units: 36km/h to m/s gives 10m/s. Write square and cubic target units as cm2/cm² and cm3/cm³; the suffix is automatically shown as a superscript. cm^2 and cm^3 are not alternative target-unit spellings; use cm² and cm³. To continue arithmetic after to, write (36km/h to m/s) * 2. With the tighter operator, write (36km/h)::m/s * 2 for the same scope. A target contains no numerical factors or arithmetic sum. The next to or :: starts another conversion step. Existing precedence, supported dimensions, numeral-system targets and UTC targets remain unchanged.
help.completion.unitContextRule: Unit suggestions continue the letters you have typed and respect the operation and constraints from surrounding parentheses. After m, square and cubic metre completions appear as m² and m³ when those units fit. In 1cm + 2m…, time, area and volume do not fit the length being added. The same length constraint applies inside 1cm + (2m… * 3). A time divisor may still fit a length calculation. If context is incomplete, keep all prefix continuations that cannot yet be ruled out. After to or ::, offer targets compatible with at least one valid interpretation: after 1m to, cm and s are possible. Selecting a target adds its constraint. Insert the visible spelling without a hidden type choice, and do not duplicate identical inserted spellings.

settings.dimming.label: Dim secondary text
settings.numberFormat.label: Number format
settings.language.englishFallback: English is used when a translation is unavailable.
settings.shortcuts.standardEditing: Standard editing shortcuts keep their usual behavior.
help.interface.managementRule: Open the application menu from the empty palette background or its tray/menu-bar icon. Use Ctrl+, on Windows or Cmd+, on Mac for settings. Right-clicking text keeps the editing menu.
help.interface.modeRule: Use Ctrl+Shift+Enter on Windows or Cmd+Shift+Enter on Mac to expand or return. Expanding starts a new sheet with the quick expression on its first line. Returning preserves the sheet and restores your previous quick draft.
help.completion.insertionRule: Suggestions match the beginning of a name without regard to case, then insert its declared spelling. Compatible local names come first, followed by your global definitions and built-ins; each group uses stable alphabetical order. Tab replaces the whole current identifier. Existing function parentheses and arguments are preserved. F1 opens the selected suggestion’s full description, or general help when no suggestion is selected. Escape restores focus.
settings.updates.label: Update checks
help.calculation.complexityRule: A recalculation has up to 500 ms, including dependencies and alternative meanings. Ready answers appear immediately. If time runs out, the calculation is cancelled and any late answer is ignored. Simplify the expression or its dependencies and try again. Your input and completed independent results remain available.
help.numeric.lowerMagnitudeRule: The smallest nonzero working magnitude is 10^(-1000), inclusive. A smaller nonzero value produces Number too small. Values within this range may display as approximately zero while remaining nonzero in later calculations: 10^(-50) * 10^25 * 10^25 = 1. Zero is allowed separately. Working precision remains 30 significant digits.
settings.systemIcon.hideWhenClosed: Hide icon when calculator is closed
settings.systemIcon.label: System icon
help.calculation.failureRule: After an internal failure, the calculator restarts its calculation engine and keeps your input and open sheet. The failed calculation is not retried automatically. Edit the expression to start a new attempt.

data.recovery.damaged: Saved data could not be read
data.recovery.preserveError: Could not preserve the original files. Data unchanged.
data.version.tooNew: Update the app to open this data
data.version.migrationFailed: Could not update the data format
data.version.returnHelp: How to return to a compatible version
help.data.recoveryRule: If saved data are damaged, choose an available backup by its date and contents, or explicitly start with empty data. The calculator preserves the original files separately before replacement. When the current state cannot be read, its differences from a backup cannot be shown accurately. If the original files cannot be preserved, recovery does not replace them.
help.data.versionRule: Before changing the data format, the calculator saves a protective backup. If the change fails, the original data remain available and the app shows how to return to a compatible version. An older app asks you to update before opening newer data and does not rewrite them.
